title: Ethics & Limits
Insight. Not absolute truth.
intro: Behind every comment is a person. VerdictLab helps explore public conversations—not judge individuals, diagnose emotions, or speak for everyone.

principles.title: Respect context
principles.description: A sample is not the whole public.

responsibleUse.title: Useful for exploration. Not every decision.
responsibleUse.label: Illustrative scenarios

scenarios.title: Explore product feedback
scenarios.description: Compare themes in public feedback to identify questions worth investigating.
scenarios.boundary: The sample describes the collected conversation—not all customers. Read original comments before drawing conclusions.
scenarios.nextStep: Report the source, collection window, sample size, and model limitations alongside the findings.

scenarios.title: Analyse mixed languages
scenarios.description: Explore English, Malay, slang, or code-switching in a conversation.
scenarios.boundary: English-oriented tools may miss local meaning. Similar model scores do not establish multilingual accuracy.
scenarios.nextStep: Review examples with people who understand the language and validate performance on a relevant labelled dataset.

scenarios.title: Judge a person
scenarios.description: Use sentiment to decide whether someone deserves a job, access to services, or a mental-health diagnosis.
scenarios.boundary: Sentiment scores do not measure character, suitability, or mental health. Do not use them for high-stakes decisions about individuals.
scenarios.nextStep: Use an appropriate human-led, accountable process instead. Do not turn exploratory scores into personal labels.

scenarios.title: Claim public consensus
scenarios.description: Treat a positive conversation on one platform as proof that everyone supports a policy.
scenarios.boundary: Online samples have platform and participation bias. A collected conversation is not a representative public-opinion survey.
scenarios.nextStep: Describe only the observed sample. Use representative research before making population-wide claims.

privacy.title: Remove identifiers. Keep your judgment.
privacy.sideNote:
Automatic redaction reduces exposure.
It cannot guarantee anonymity.
privacy.subheading: Less personal data. Less avoidable risk.
privacy.description: The reference pipeline redacts supported email, phone, and handle patterns and replaces URLs. Names, locations, and indirect identifying details can still remain.
guidance: Check source permissions and platform requirements.
Do not upload sensitive or private conversations.
Review text before sharing examples or results.
privacy.original: “I’m Maya, the only librarian in Pinebridge. Contact maya@example.com or @maya_demo. The update keeps crashing.”
privacy.redacted: “I’m Maya, the only librarian in Pinebridge. Contact [email] or [handle]. The update keeps crashing.”
privacy.warning: The name and unique role still identify someone. Removing an email and handle is not enough.
privacy.footnote: Synthetic example · Not a live redaction tool

boundaries.title: What the result cannot promise.
boundaries.sideNote:
Limits belong alongside the findings.
Not hidden in the small print.

items.title: Sarcasm & context
items.why: Positive words can express negative intent. All three models can agree and still be wrong.
items.action: Read the original comment and surrounding conversation. Treat disagreement as a reason to investigate, not a correction.

items.title: Language & cultural bias
items.why: English-oriented tools can misread Malay, code-switching, slang, and community-specific expressions.
items.action: Validate on relevant language samples and include reviewers who understand the community.

items.title: Sampling & representation
items.why: Platform choice, collection dates, missing records, and who chooses to post all shape the result.
items.action: Describe the collected sample and its gaps. Do not extrapolate to the entire public.

items.title: Confidence & emotion
items.why: Confidence labels are heuristic, not calibrated probabilities. Emotion dimensions are exploratory, not diagnoses.
items.action: Report sample size and model agreement separately. Do not interpret an emotion score as fact about a person.

items.title: Privacy & redaction
items.why: Supported patterns can be redacted, but names, locations, and indirect identifiers may remain.
items.action: Avoid sensitive uploads and review text manually. Publicly visible does not mean risk-free or unrestricted to reuse.

items.title: Validation & accuracy
items.why: The reference project includes sentiment evaluation: this preview claims no measured benchmark result.
items.action: Use measured results from relevant data before claiming performance. A sentiment benchmark does not validate emotion dimensions.
